title: Simultaneous Equations and Inequalities
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Equations and Inequalities Worksheets
standard_text: Solve simultaneous equations in two variables by elimination and by substitution, including one linear and one quadratic equation; solve linear and quadratic inequalities and express solutions in set notation.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on simultaneous equations (one linear, one quadratic), linear inequalities and quadratic inequalities. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Substitute the linear equation into the quadratic.
key_sub: For a quadratic inequality, find the critical values and sketch.
body_html:
How it works

To solve y = x² + … and y = mx + c, set them equal and solve the quadratic. Each x gives a point of intersection.

Solving inequalities is like solving equations, but multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the sign.

Example

Solve y = x² and y = x + 2.

x² − x − 2 = 0

(x − 2)(x + 1) = 0

Answer: x = 2 or x = −1

Example

Solve 5 − 2x > 11.

−2x > 6

Divide by −2 and reverse

Answer: x < −3

Common mistakes

  • Not reversing the inequality after dividing by a negative.
  • Finding x but not the matching y-values.
  • Squaring both sides of an inequality.

faq.q: How do you solve one linear and one quadratic equation?
faq.a: Make y (or x) the subject of the linear one, substitute into the quadratic, then solve the quadratic.

faq.q: When does an inequality sign change direction?
faq.a: When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number.
